findings.detail: lstat plus later O_RDONLY open can open a replaced special inode before fstat rejection. No read follows a rejected fstat, but block_devices_opened:false is unconditional. Trusted genuine sysfs makes this implausible; adversarial fixtures are not fully race-proof.
findings.suggestion: Pin O_PATH descriptor, validate regular type, then reopen verified descriptor for read; or explicitly narrow input trust/claim.

findings.detail: getpid()==1 alone does not prove root is an initramfs. mkdir proc/sys could modify disk-root metadata in another deployment, despite unconditional writes_to_storage:false.
findings.suggestion: Check RAMFS_MAGIC/TMPFS_MAGIC with statfs before PID1 mkdir/mount, or narrow intended-deployment claim.

confirmed: No write/open flag or mount source targets raw storage in the intended initramfs path.
SD and MMC roles remain candidates; no record approves a write target or claims boot-medium identity.
No flash/format/reboot backend or interactive shell is implemented.
Mounts are proc/sysfs only with read-only/nosuid/nodev/noexec.
Read-meta byte bound, decimal overflow handling and JSON escaping are present.
limits: No PID1/kernel/initramfs boot, mount execution, physical hardware, drivers or internal preservation demonstrated.
Fixture execution is not a security sandbox; class/block parent symlinks are intentionally traversed for real sysfs compatibility.
scandir allocates before entry-count rejection; use trusted kernel/finite test trees rather than assuming a memory-bound adversarial directory reader.
